raw_answer_text:
A1: It is broadcast to every station on the segment.
A2: It lacks a mapping between the target host's IP (protocol) address and its hardware (MAC) address in its ARP table.
A3: It stores the sender's protocol (IP) address together with the sender's hardware (MAC) address.
A4: No, only the intended target host replies; other hosts silently discard or ignore the request.
A5: It is sent directly (unicast) to just the requesting host, not broadcast.
A6: It caches the target's IP-to-MAC mapping in its ARP table and can then send the originally intended packet directly to that hardware address.
A7: It does not know the target's hardware address; obtaining that address is exactly the purpose of the request.
A8: It merges the sender's mapping into its table before checking whether the opcode is a request or a reply.
